proposed.why: The evidence agrees: the provider stopped answering at about 02:42, and our 503s and slow requests follow directly from that.

diagnosis.hypothesis: fake-provider, which stands for the outside payment provider, suddenly stopped answering POST /v1/payments and /v1/refunds at about 02:42. Its container still reports running and healthy, so it is hanging rather than down. payments-api gives each provider call 3 s and tries 3 times, so each request now takes about 9 to 16 s and then returns 503 ('provider unavailable; payment left pending'). That produces the 74% 5xx rate and the 10 s p95. Before the stall, provider calls returned 200 in about 5 ms (p95), with occasional 500s, so the change was abrupt rather than a gradual overload. No deploy lines up with it: the whole stack was created at 02:39:46. payments-api's own health check now fails, probably because its workers are tied up waiting on the provider; I did not confirm this. Still open: why the provider stalled, which we cannot see from our side. Also open: whether the timed-out requests reached the provider and were charged there. I did not run the money check.

evidence.shows: POST /payments: 201s fall from about 2.5/s to 0 and 503s jump to about 2.5/s at 02:42:09, confirming the alert.
payments-api's completed provider calls (200 at about 3/s, 500 at about 0.2/s) drop to 0 at 02:42:12. The provider stopped responding.
Every recent payments-api ERROR reads 'provider unavailable; payment/refund left pending' with '/v1/payments (or /v1/refunds) failed after 3 attempts: ReadTimeout'. This starts at 02:42:09.

Trace for pmt_000276: three POSTs to fake-provider /v1/payments each hit ReadTimeout after about 3.0 s, the request took 15.9 s and returned 503. Redis and Postgres spans took under 1 ms, so they are not the cause.
Provider-call p95 was steady at about 5 ms through 02:42:05, then has no data: a sudden stall with no gradual slowdown before it.
All containers were created together at 02:39:46. No deploy or settings change coincides with the 02:42 onset.
fake-provider is running and healthy with 0 restarts, so it is hung rather than crashed. payments-api is unhealthy: its health-check request fails.

proposed_fix.target: fake-provider (external payment provider) and the payments-api provider client
proposed_fix.summary: Escalate to the provider: their payments and refunds API is hanging. On our side, stop requests piling up while it lasts: add a circuit breaker or fail fast on provider timeouts instead of the 3 x 3 s retry loop, so payments-api stays responsive and its health check recovers. Do not retry pending payments under new idempotency keys. When the provider recovers, reconcile every payment and refund left pending since 02:42 against the provider's records and webhooks, keeping the same idempotency keys. Then run money_check to confirm our books match the provider's.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Failing fast affects every payment and refund while the breaker is open. Callers get 503 sooner, and payments that might have succeeded on a slow provider get rejected. Reconciling pending rows changes payment and refund state. If it is done without idempotency keys or provider lookups, it risks double charges or missed ledger postings.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Revert the breaker or timeout change to the previous retry and timeout settings and restart payments-api. Reconcile only from the provider's records. Change nothing on the provider's side, and leave rows pending if their state is unclear.
